title: Noise embargo and incident decelerator with autoremediation harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a multi-layered alerting dampener and staged incident decelerator that reduces noisy pages during transient SLO violations while enabling automated containment and rapid human escalation for severe, persistent degradations. The solution couples: (1) a short-term "embargo" window for low-severity signals derived from SLO trend detectors, (2) region-aware circuit-breakers to prevent noisy cascading failovers, and (3) a runbook recommendation and autoremediation harness that can automatically execute safe remediation steps (cache-clears, traffic steering to healthy pools) and escalate when thresholds persist. This ticket covers design, implementation, simulation harness, and a staged rollout with telemetry-driven guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Noise rate (pages/hour) for non-critical routes reduced by >=60% in synthetic surge tests without increasing mean time to repair for true incidents
Embargo logic correctly suppresses alerts for transient single-region latency spikes under configured SLO grace windows
Circuit-breaker prevents cross-region failover amplification in simulated region-degradation scenarios
Autoremediation actions have opt-out flag and require explicit approval for actions that are not idempotent
End-to-end e2e simulation runbook and dashboard created with pass/fail metrics and runbook audit logs visible in Console
